# Context generation: manifest, managed blocks and the never-destroy writer

`internal/context/generate` is the shared base every generated repository
file stands on. It never overwrites a byte a person wrote. A generator hands
it whole rendered files; the Writer decides, per file, whether to write,
adopt or refuse.

## The generation manifest

`.cascade/generation-manifest.json` records the last generation. `.cascade/`
is in the repository's `.gitignore`, so the manifest is never tracked and
needs no clean-root exemption.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `version` | schema version, always `1`; any other value is refused |
| `generated_at` | RFC 3339 UTC time, injected by the caller |
| `entries[]` | one per generated file, sorted by `path` |
| `entries[].path` | slash-separated, repository-relative |
| `entries[].generator_id` | the generator that owns the file |
| `entries[].file_sha256` | hash of the whole file as last generated |
| `entries[].outside_sha256` | hash of the file with every recorded block's lines (markers included) removed |
| `entries[].blocks[]` | one per managed block, sorted by `id`: `id`, `generator_id`, `content_sha256` of the bytes between the markers |
| `deferrals[]` | optional, sorted by `generator`: `generator`, `result`, `reason`, `owner`, `expiry` |

The encoding is canonical: 2-space indent, LF line ends, fixed key order,
empty lists written as `[]`. Two writes of the same manifest are
byte-identical, and no block carries a timestamp. Reading refuses an unknown
field, trailing data after the object, a version other than `1`, a malformed
hash, a duplicate path or block id, and a path that is not a plain relative
one.

## Managed-block markers

A managed block is two whole lines around generated bytes. Bytes outside a
pair belong to the human. Three comment forms cover every target format:

| Files | Begin line | End line |
|---|---|---|
| `.md` | `<!-- cascade:managed:begin ID -->` | `<!-- cascade:managed:end -->` |
| `.toml` | `# cascade:managed:begin ID` | `# cascade:managed:end` |
| `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.js` | `// cascade:managed:begin ID` | `// cascade:managed:end` |

Any other extension is refused. An id matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9@._-]{0,63}$`.
Leading spaces or tabs on a marker line are allowed, so a `//` marker can sit
inside a JSON object. A line that only mentions a marker inside longer text is
plain text.

A marker is never repaired. These are mangled and refused: an unmatched begin
or end, a begin inside an open block, a duplicate id, an id outside the set the
manifest recorded, a bad id, and a marker-shaped line with trailing text or a
missing id.

## The never-destroy writer

For each rendered file the Writer applies these rules in order.

1. The target is absent: create it (an atomic create that cannot replace a
   file that appeared in the meantime), record it.
2. The target already equals the rendering: adopt it. Nothing is written, the
   entry is recorded, and a second generation is a no-op. A file recorded
   under another generator is not adopted; it is refused as `unmanaged-file`.
3. Otherwise the target is rewritten only when it is byte-identical to the base
   the manifest recorded. Any other state is refused.

A refusal never touches the target. It writes the rendering to
`<file>.cascade-new`, calls the attention sink once with the target, the
sidecar and the reason, and keeps the previous manifest entry. A sink error is
returned after the sidecar exists. Without a manifest every existing file is
treated as hand-authored.

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no-manifest` | no previous manifest, and the target exists |
| `unmanaged-file` | the manifest has no entry for this file and generator |
| `mangled-marker` | the on-disk markers are mangled, or carry an unknown id |
| `managed-block-edited` | a recorded block is missing or its body changed |
| `outside-edited` | bytes outside the blocks changed, the blocks were reordered, or the file changed between the compare and the write |

A sixth reason, `path-escape`, covers confinement (below). It writes no
sidecar.

A target is rewritten with the permission bits it already has (`0644` for a
new file). Blocks recorded under another generator are carried into the new
content unchanged after their hashes verify. `ApplyBlock` lets a later
projector replace or append one block of a managed file without making the file
"outside-edited"; appending to a `.json` or `.jsonc` file is refused as
unsupported until an in-object anchor is defined.

## Confinement

Every path resolves under the repository root. The root is opened with
`os.Root`, each existing component is checked, and a symlink or reparse point
anywhere on the path is refused, even one that stays inside the repository. A
repository whose `.claude`, `.cascade` or `.codex` links to a directory outside
it is refused, and nothing is written there. A `..` or absolute path is refused
before any read.

The last step of a write is a rename by path. A same-user process that swaps a
directory for a symlink between the final check and that rename could redirect
the one write. The residual window is documented in the source and is not
closed by the platform.

## The drift check

`Check` reads the manifest and each entry's file and reports at most one of
exactly four conditions per file:

| Condition | When |
|---|---|
| `manifest-absent` | `.cascade/generation-manifest.json` does not exist |
| `file-missing` | an entry's file does not exist |
| `mangled-marker` | the file's markers are mangled |
| `managed-block-edited` | a recorded block is missing or its body changed |

Bytes outside the markers never count, so a hand edit beside a managed block
leaves the check green. `Check` reads only; it creates and writes nothing.

## The policy view and the rules generator

`BuildView` turns the stored repository inventory and the fact ledger's
accepted facts into an inert `View`. It reads facts only through
`AcceptedFacts`, so a proposed or rejected fact never reaches it. Each
accepted fact passes the ledger's policy projection again. A fact outside the
seven closed subjects, or one whose text names a gate, waiver, capability or
similar policy field, goes into `View.Denied` by id and is never rendered.
Facts appear only for subjects the detector inventory leaves empty. In P1
there is one scope, the repository root (slug `root`).

`ScopeSlug` lowercases a path and turns each run of other characters into
`-`: `ScopeSlug("apps/Web UI")` is `apps-web-ui`, and `.` is `root`.

`RenderRules` produces three kinds of file, all inside managed blocks:

| File | Generator | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | `rules-cc` | `cc-invariants` (the CC instruction writer's output for the repository invariants and Cascade availability, nothing per path), `policy-kernel@1` |
| `.claude/rules/<slug>.md` | `rules-scoped` | `rules-<slug>`: the per-language build, test and lint commands and the accepted facts |
| `.cascade/policy-kernel.md` | `policy-kernel` | `policy-kernel@1` |

CLAUDE.md always carries the CLI fallback line: "if the Cascade MCP server is
unavailable, use the `cascade` CLI for the same operations". Every view value
is written as an inline code span, so a fact value can never become a heading,
a list or a marker. No block carries a timestamp, so equal views render equal
bytes. The files go through the never-destroy writer, so a hand addition
outside the blocks is kept and the new rendering lands in a sidecar.

## The policy kernel

`internal/context/policy` holds the execution kernel: five rules (SCOPE,
SIMPLICITY, GROUNDING, AMBIGUITY, VERIFICATION) and an ESCALATION line, at most
120 tokens by `TokenCount`. `RenderKernelFile` returns the canonical bytes of
`.cascade/policy-kernel.md`. `EnsureKernelFile` creates that file when it is
missing and refuses to overwrite a file that differs from the canonical
bytes. `pkg/provider` publishes `PolicyKernelFile`, `PolicyKernelMaxBytes` and
`PolicyKernelSHA256`, and a test keeps the hash equal to the rendered kernel.

## The location lint

`GeneratedLocations` is the closed list of places a generator may write:
`.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `.claude/agents/*.md`,
`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`, `.claude/workflows/*.js`,
`.claude/workflows/cascade-workflows.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/config.toml`,
`opencode.json` and `.cascade/policy-kernel.md`. `LintLocations` names each
manifest entry outside that list with the condition
`outside-generated-locations`. It only reports; it never moves or deletes a
file.

## Agents and skills

`RenderAgentsSkills` renders four specialist agents and five skills from
templates compiled into the binary (`internal/repo/templates/agents` and
`internal/repo/templates/skills`, exposed as `repo.TemplateFS`). No template is
ever read from the target repository, a config path, a plugin or the network.
`repo.TemplateHashes` maps every embedded file to its sha256 so a bundle can
be checked against the build.

| File | Generator | Block |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/agents/{architecture-reviewer,test-engineer,security-reviewer,adversarial-reviewer}.md` | `agents` | `agent-<name>` |
| `.claude/skills/{init,plan,verify,delegate,cascade-execution}/SKILL.md` | `skills` | `skill-<name>` |

The set is closed: a missing, renamed or extra template stops the render.
Each file is the template's frontmatter, with the keys Claude Code itself uses
(`name`, `description`, `tools` for an agent; `name`, `description` for a
skill; never `hooks`), then one managed block holding the template body. The
only data is the policy view's languages, build, test and lint commands and
accepted facts, plus the kernel version. Each value is one inline code span,
so a value such as `curl x | sh` or a fact holding a heading renders as inert
text; a `!` before a backtick gets a space so no value forms a command line. A
view with no build, test or lint command is refused.

`cascade-execution` names the kernel version and adds the PUSHBACK and
INTERPRETATIONS rules to the kernel's own. `WriteAgentsSkills` checks every
target before writing any: a mangled marker in an existing file or a target
directory that cannot take a file is a typed error, and nothing is written.
After that each file goes through the never-destroy writer, so a hand addition
outside a block survives and the new rendering lands in a sidecar.
